newsitem.title: UK: UK Liberal Democrats to vote against tax cut.
newsitem.headline: UK Liberal Democrats to vote against tax cut.

text.p: Britain's minority Liberal Democrats will vote against a proposed one point cut in the basic rate of income tax to 23 percent, party leader Paddy Ashdown said.

"That's what we believe to be right and we're the only party who's done it before," he told BBC radio a day after Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke had revealed his budget.

"We really can't go on lying to the electorate like this. Both the Chancellor and the shadow Chancellor know perfectly well that they ought to be investing in education, that they ought to be reducing the debt and that they ought not to be handing out tax cuts," he said.
Ashdown predicted that the next government would claw back the tax cuts handed out by Clarke.

"Within 14 months inflation will start to rise and everyone will be telling us to tighten our belts...I expect that by the turn of the year, interest rates will go up.That is very very bad news," he said.
